The Treaty of Resht was signed on January 21, 1732, between the Russian Empire and the Safavid Empire. The treaty marked a significant shift in power dynamics. Russia agreed to relinquish its claims south of the Kura River, including parts of Gilan, Mazandaran, and Astarabad that had been seized by Peter I during his early reign. This was accompanied by the Iranian cities of Derbent, Tarki, Ganja, etc., north of the Kura river being returned to Russia within three years.

In exchange, Iran granted trade privileges to Russian merchants. Additionally, Iran promised to restore Georgian king Vakhtang VI on the throne of Kartli as soon as Ottoman forces were expelled from Georgia. The treaty was confirmed by the 1735 Treaty of Ganja, where all regions north of the Kura river were returned.

For more details about this historical event, you can refer to Wikipedia articles: "Treaty of Resht" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Resht).
